title: Kuikúro language
extract: Kuikúro, also known as Amonap, Upper Xingu Cariban and Apalakiri, is a Cariban language spoken by the Kuikuro and Kalapalo peoples of Brazil. It is spoken in seven villages along the Culuene River in the Xingu Indigenous Park of Mato Grosso. The Matipuhy language, closely related and sometimes considered a distinct language, is moribund, with only 10 speakers remaining.
